newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam minister urges tight party, police ties.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam minister urges tight party, police ties.

text.p: Vietnam's Interior Minister Le Minh Huong has urged a further reinforcing of Communist Party control in the national police force to help defend Hanoi against threats including subversion.

Huong, one of the country's most powerful politicians and a member of the elite Politburo, told a meeting of top police officials last Saturday that work to build the party within the police force was a key task.

Tuesday's official Nhan Dan daily quoted him as saying a strong, clean police force under the absolute and direct control of the party would "contribute to the cause of defending the Party, the regime and the people".
Huong's remarks were in line with broader moves, unveiled at a landmark party Congress last June, aimed at heightening the role of the national security mechanism in official policy.
Government officials have warned repeatedly that Vietnam is under threat from groups and individuals seeking to undermine its communist government through various means, including peaceful evolution.
The Interior Ministry, which controls the police force, is charged with maintaining internal security and party loyalty. It is arguably the most powerful government organ in Vietnam.
